result.title: Same Rank, Different Needs: Rethinking LoRA Redistribution in Federated Learning
result.summary: Federated low-rank adaptation (LoRA) enables clients with different resource budgets to collaboratively fine-tune foundation models. To distribute an aggregated update within each client's rank budget, existing methods commonly retain its leading singular directions. However, directions that best reconstruct the update matrix need not best preserve its responses on a particular client's inputs: a lower-energy direction may matter more to that recipient. We formalize this mismatch and show that matrix-optimal truncation can incur arbitrarily larger response error than another readout of the same rank. Motivated by this result, we propose Receiver-Aware Subspace Adaptation (RASA), a plug-in framework for receiver-aware knowledge transfer. RASA uses compact diagonal input second moments to perform uncentered PCA of receiver-weighted update responses. The resulting readout is globally optimal for the rank-constrained receiver objective and preserves at least as much response energy as spectral truncation under the diagonal metric. RASA also introduces spectral-reference aggregation, which removes the personalized initialization offset while retaining the locally learned increment. Experiments on DomainNet-100, NICO++, GLUE, and SuperNI demonstrate RASA's effectiveness across methods under resource, task, and data heterogeneity. In particular, RASA improves DomainNet-100 accuracy by 3.23 percentage points with FlexLoRA and achieves gains of up to 8.33 ROUGE-L points on seen SuperNI tasks and 4.37 on unseen tasks with modest overhead.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究联邦 LoRA 中聚合更新如何按各客户端的秩预算重新分配，指出保留最大奇异方向（重构最优）未必保留该接收方输入上的响应，并提出用输入二阶矩加权的无中心 PCA 得到接收方感知的子空间读出 RASA。
AI.relevance_reason: 「低秩截断按矩阵重构最优、却可能大幅放大任务响应误差」这一分析，与 LVR 中 latent 状态压缩、视觉信息坍缩以及按任务必要信息筛选子空间的问题可能相通，其对角度量下的最优读出可供核查迁移。
